summary: This FYI memo is a short bibliography of recent resources to help a network novice learn about the Internet, including its networks, resources, protocols, and history. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This is a short reading list for people who are new to the Internet.

questions: how do beginners learn about the internet
subtitle: A curated reading list for Internet newcomers.

tldr.problem: New Internet users needed guidance on where to find introductory information about networks, the Internet, protocols, and connectivity.
tldr.mechanism: This FYI memo collects a short bibliography of recent books, papers and online resources organized by topic: introductory papers, Internet services, networks, protocols, and further reading.
tldr.outcome: The RFC serves as a quick reference guide that network service providers and user support staff could hand to novices, with pointers to both free online documents and published books.

today: RFC 1463 is an informational document that served its time well, providing guidance to Internet novices in the early 1990s. While the specific resources and publishers mentioned have changed, the document remains a historical example of how the Internet community supported new users, and the principle of curating learning resources for different skill levels remains relevant.

sections.title: A Bibliography for the Network Novice
sections.content: RFC 1463 is a brief bibliography designed specifically for people new to the Internet. It lists resources to help newcomers understand networks, the Internet, protocols, and how to connect. The memo organizes materials into categories: introductory papers, books about using the Internet, guides to getting connected, information about Internet services and resources, and further reading for those who need more detailed information. The RFC is intentionally concise so it can be used as a handout by user support personnel.
sections.plainLanguage: This RFC is a list of good books and papers for someone just learning about the Internet, organized by topic.

sections.title: Resource Categories
sections.content: The bibliography includes several categories of resources. Introductory papers include Brendan Kehoe's Zen and the Art of the Internet and Ed Hoffman's What is the Internet?. The RFC lists books on using the Internet, including guides from O'Reilly and Prentice Hall. It covers how to find Internet connectivity and get started. It includes sections on Internet services, resources for exploring the network, information about Internet networks themselves, and technical introductions to Internet protocols like TCP/IP. The memo marks materials available for free online with an asterisk, so users without resources for books know what they can obtain immediately.
sections.plainLanguage: The list has books about learning the Internet, guides on how to connect, explanations of how networks work, and places to find online papers.

sections.title: Accessing Online Resources
sections.content: The RFC provides practical guidance on how to access the free online documents listed in the bibliography. Many resources are available via Anonymous FTP from sites including nic.merit.edu, nic.mr.net, ftp.nisc.sri.com, and ftp.hawaii.edu. The Access Guide contains location information and instructions. For those without direct Internet access, the memo explains how to retrieve documents through dial-up services using a modem. The RFC notes that local network service providers often publish additional guides and newsletters with Internet learning materials, so consulting one's own provider is recommended.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC tells you where to download the free papers on the Internet, and how to get them even with just a modem.
